previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of chronic systolic heart failure, ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for shortness of breath and chest pain following a recent pacemaker implantation. He reported noncompliance with medications due to financial constraints. Evaluation revealed uncontrolled hypertension with a blood pressure of 153/112 mmHg, but no evidence of acute coronary syndrome. His symptoms improved with optimization of antihypertensive therapy, including restarting lisinopril at 20mg daily and adjusting hydralazine dosing to improve adherence. His heart failure was stable, with mild residual pulmonary edema on imaging and euvolemic status on exam. He was monitored for device function, which remained normal, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up to monitor renal function and medication management.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo male with dilated cardiomyopathy, EF 35% who admitted with 
palpitations and shortness of breath in the setting of 
medication nonadherance due to financial issues.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Acute on chronic systolic CHF exacerbation: This exacerbation 
was likely provoked by dietary noncompliance ___ food) and 
poor medication adherence in setting of inability to afford 
medications. His most recent echo from ___ showed EF of 
35%. He has had thorough work ups during previous 
hospitalizations, including cardiac catheterization with only 
60% circumflex lesion that was not thought to be responsible for 
his cardiomyopathy. On admission, pt was restarted on his home 
dose of torsemide 40 mg, with effective diuresis and improvement 
in his shortness of breath. Upon discharge, pt was transitioned 
from torsemide to furosemide given financial concerns. He was 
continued on his home blood pressure medications and afterload 
reduction with lisinopril, spironolactone, hydralazine and 
Imdur. Weight on discharged was 138 kg.

# Tachy-brady syndrome: On admission, pt had ICD interrogated 
which revealed NSVT but no evidence of ICD fire. His 
palpitations were attributed to these episodes in the setting of 
non-adherence to his metoprolol. He was restarted on his home 
metoprolol dose on admission with resolution of his 
palpitations. 

CHRONIC ISSUES:
# CAD: Patient with known non obstructive CAD (proximal 60% 
LCX), no evidence of active ACS on admission. He was continued 
on medical management with aspirin, beta blockade, ace inhibitor 
and Imdur. 

# Hypertension: Pt's blood pressure remained well controlled on 
his home regimen.  

# Diabetes type 2 with neuropathy: He was continued on his home 
dose of Lantus. 
 
# HLD:  Continued statin

# CKD:  Creatinine remained stable at 1.4-1.5.

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
Pt was seen by social work while in house given financial issues 
regarding obtaining his medications. He was granted a 14 day 
free supply of medications through the free care pharmacy, 
however this is only a temporary solution as he is not eligible 
to continuous free care given that he has health insurance 
coverage. Pt was advised to follow up with social work as an 
outpatient. His PCP and outpatient cardiologist were also 
contacted regarding these financial issues.
